title: Sephiria Characters — Hero, Costumes & Tower NPCs (1.0)
description: Sephiria characters guide: the playable rabbit hero, how costumes change opening stats, and the village and tower NPCs that gate weapons and secret skins.
meta: Covers sephiria characters / NPC searches; pairs with the costume roster page.
body:
Sephiria has one playable hero — the rabbit — plus a roster of costumes that change how a run starts. Everyone else is an NPC, and two of them gate weapon unlocks and a secret costume.

Who you play

You play the rabbit of Bunnyville. There is no class pick and no second hero, so your real character choice is the costume — and costumes are not cosmetic, because each one trades opening stats against each other. That makes them behave like a pre-run loadout rather than a skin.

How costumes change a run

  • Costumes set opening stats and trade-offs, so they shift which build comes online fastest — see builds.
  • Some are unlocked by challenges rather than bought. The costume roster page lists every skin with its effect and unlock condition.
  • Roster size depends on when you count: the launch listing says over 20 costumes, while the community database tracked at v1.0.24 lists 27 playable skins (8 from the start, 19 unlocked).

Non-playable characters

CharacterWhereWhat they do
Moro (written Morrow in some guides)Village training ground, east sideUnlocks weapon branches once you own the matching Destiny Inscription node. Community data lists Greatsword, Dagger, Crossbow, Blade and Staff on this route, with Sword and Shield excluded
Manok, the friendly wandererVillage, at the Iron MaidenRuns the Blood Donation event; donating five times across runs unlocks the Wingless Bat costume
ElruHides in three spots: the carrot farm, the pond by the clothing shop, and the Ark puzzle roomThe Hide and Seek event target, and a repeatable Destiny Inscription event
HizoNear the farmVillage event NPC
ConnorIn front of the ArkVillage event NPC
ValterMagic WorkshopVillage event NPC
NPC roles and locations come from community records, including the in-game Destiny Inscription event text. If a village event has moved in a patch, your client wins.
